q: The electric field between the plates is ____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric field between the plates is uniform.

q: Suppose that the electric field intensity between the parallel plates is ____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. Suppose that the electric field intensity between the parallel plates is E.

q: Consider a ____ between the two plates.
e: Consider a unit positive charge between the two plates. Unit positive charge is what this statement is using.

q: Therefore, the force acting upon a unit positive charge is ____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Therefore, the force acting upon a unit positive charge is E.

q: The work done in bringing the charge from B to A against that force is $W = $ ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work done in bringing the charge from B to A against that force is W = Ed.

q: Since this work done is the electric potential difference V between the two plates, $V = $ ____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Since this work done is the electric potential difference V between the two plates, V = W.

q: Therefore the relation between potential difference and the electric field intensity between two plates is ____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. Therefore the relation between potential difference and the electric field intensity between two plates is V = Ed.

q: The unit of electric field intensity is also expressed in ____ according to Eq(9.10).
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The unit of electric field intensity is also expressed in volt per metre (V m^-1) according to Eq(9.10).

q: Parallel charged plates are two parallel metal plates of same size and same material, carrying charges of ____ separated by a distance.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Parallel charged plates are two parallel metal plates of same size and same material, carrying charges of equal magnitude and opposite signs separated by a distance.
